newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Loyola says no credit curbs planned.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Loyola says no credit curbs planned.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said there were no plans to adopt credit restrictions at an upcoming policy-makers meeting, but he did not rule them out entirely.

"There is nothing scheduled for the next meeting of the National Monetary Council regarding credit restrictions. We are monitoring the economy and if restrictive measures are necessary we will adopt them," he told reporters at a seminar on banking in Sao Paulo.
The council meets next on April 24.
Loyola's comments come amid increasing market speculation of an imminent move by authorities to restrict consumer credit in a bid to curb imports, which are pressuring external accounts.
They also follow a decision this week by the Central Bank to leave May interest rates unchanged from April's 1.58 percent, ending an eight-month policy of rate reductions.
Loyola was quoted Friday by InvestNews as saying the decision to leave rates unchanged should not signal "alarm."
"By keeping rates the same, the government is only trying to signal to the markets a tendency toward stabilization," Loyola was quoted as saying.
